justification: Assessment reports INVALID at line 0157/0158, the step asserting chi(n) is nonnegative for all n <= X. This is exactly the ground-truth flaw ('If X is the largest integer for which coefficients of f and its twist agree for n <= X, then chi(n) is nonnegative for every n <= X'). The assessment correctly explains why the claim fails: the definition of X only forces chi(n) = 1 where lambda_f(n) != 0, leaving n with lambda_f(n) = 0 (supersingular primes, etc.) free to have chi(n) = -1. The ground-truth witness (eta(3t)^2 eta(9t)^2 with a_2 = 0, chi = (./5), chi(2) = -1) is a concrete instance of the same phenomenon; the assessment's witness class (n coprime to q with lambda_f(n) = 0 and chi(n) = -1) is a valid alternative witness for the same claim. Same defect, so CAUGHT_MATCHING.
